Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: P2P digital transfers are supported via mobile money: UNCDF report notes CBOS licenses mobile money operators to provide mobile payment services and manage wallets, and that MMOs are integrated into the national switch/payment system (EBS), enabling wallet-based transfers.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed on fresher, primary evidence: Bank of Khartoum's Bankak app supports transfers between own accounts, other bank accounts and mobile-money wallets, and The New Humanitarian (Feb 2024) reports 7 million users with an 85% rise in app activations since the 2023 war began; Al-Monitor (Jan 2025) confirms continued reliance on apps like Bankak for transfers despite conflict. Value Code 2 (Yes) stands, upgraded from a single weak source to authoritative, current evidence.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: UNCDF’s Sudan Payment Infrastructure Assessment describes a national retail payments switch (Electronic Banking Service Company, EBS) with all 38 banks connected as direct participants and interoperable with mobile money operators, plus SRAG RTGS (launched 2008, mandatory for banks) and Electronic Cheque Clearing (ECC, launched 2006, integrated with SRAG). It also notes mobile money operators licensed by CBOS and integrated into the national switch, but no evidence of a modern 24/7 instant retail payment system; cross-border connectivity is absent.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate. Comment wording may not match the score — re-read (needs judgement).
revision_notes: Material change since the 2023 source: FSD Africa's rapid assessment (2024/25) finds the EBS national switch that the original evidence relied on has been down since the war began, is not expected to be restored medium-term, and only 5-6 of 37 banks remain operational, with interbank settlement now done manually by cheque; CBOS only opened a public tender for a genuine National Instant Payments System (NIPS) in April 2026, confirming no unified instant system yet exists. However bank-led apps (Bankak, Fawry) continue to provide real instant P2P/P2B functionality to millions of users. Value Code kept at 4 (Partially deployed) to reflect this siloed bank-led functionality, but the basis has changed substantially and this is flagged for human review given the collapse of national interoperability.
